architecture.mechanism: An empirically grounded agent-based Monte Carlo model (EMB) that derives empirical bus velocity distributions and exponential passenger inter-arrival distributions from GPS positional/temporal data, reproducing the stochastic dynamics that cause bunching, so that rule-based control strategies — holding, no-boarding, and centralized-pulsing — can be evaluated and applied to equalize headways.
architecture.intervention: Feed the route's existing GPS traces and passenger arrival counts into the EMB model, then implement the holding rule-set (with no-boarding or centralized-pulsing as fallbacks): any bus running ahead of its target headway is held at a stop until even spacing is restored, using the model-calibrated rule-set rather than adding vehicles.
architecture.expected_effect: Headway variance on the route decreases, eliminating the three-buses-together then half-hour-gap pattern; arrivals become evenly spaced and passenger wait times stabilize with the current fleet.
architecture.falsification_test: Calibrate the EMB model on the route's own GPS logs and arrival counts, then compare simulated headway standard deviation under the holding rule-set against a no-intervention baseline; if holding fails to yield a statistically significant headway-variance reduction, or introduces a larger failure (schedule slips, stop overcrowding), the mechanism is rejected before field deployment.
